details: Raiden-baileys (a Baileys/WhatsApp socket fork) ships hidden code that makes every connected WhatsApp account follow channels chosen by the package author. In lib/Socket/newsletter.js, inside makeNewsletterSocket, an unconditional setTimeout(…, 120000) is queued when the module is loaded: after two minutes it iterates a hardcoded array of channel IDs — 120363407277177688@newsletter and 120363407702752541@newsletter — and issues a WhatsApp w:mex query with QueryIds.FOLLOW for each one, swallowing any error so the action leaves no trace in the application logs. The timer's only purpose is to move the follow request outside the window in which a bot is typically started and inspected, and to hide it behind normal startup traffic. There is no configuration option, callback, or return value for this action: it is not exposed through the socket API, cannot be disabled by the integrator, and is unrelated to the library's documented newsletter helpers (newsletterFollow/newsletterUnfollow), which take a caller-supplied JID. Any WhatsApp bot built on this package silently enrols its linked account(s) into the two hardcoded channels after start-up. Hardcoded IOCs: WhatsApp channel JIDs 120363407277177688@newsletter and 120363407702752541@newsletter. raiden-baileys 2.1.6 is a modified WhatsApp (Baileys) library that silently enrols the bot owner's WhatsApp account into hardcoded channels. lib/Socket/newsletter.js defines makeNewsletterSocket; inside it, an unexported and undelivered `setTimeout(async () => {...}, 120000)` waits two minutes and then, for each of two hardcoded channel JIDs — "120363407277177688@newsletter" and "120363407702752541@newsletter" — sends the WhatsApp newsletter FOLLOW query (query id 7871414976211147 defined in lib/Types/Newsletter.js) through the connected account. There is no corresponding unfollow and no user-facing option to disable it, so any application that builds a socket through this module makes the user's account follow channels it never chose; the two-minute delay keeps the action outside short startup observation windows. A second hardcoded channel, "120363411769951302@newsletter" (with the display name "alip shop #information"), is injected in lib/Socket/clutch-handler.js as the forwardedNewsletterMessageInfo of outgoing event messages, making this library's bot traffic advertise an unrelated channel. The package contains no credential, environment or wallet access; the payload is account manipulation and concealed channel attribution. IOCs: WhatsApp channel JIDs 120363407277177688@newsletter, 120363407702752541@newsletter, 120363411769951302@newsletter.
